4066211:rest.note: Williams (rest) is listed as out for Thursday's game versus the Bucks.
4066211:rest.long: Williams will take the night off Thursday after appearing in Portland's last five contests. He will presumably be back on the floor Saturday against the Knicks. In the meantime, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen should see more minutes behind Donovan Clingan.

4066336:wrist.name: Lauri Markkanen
4066336:wrist.note: Markkanen is out for Tuesday's game versus the Heat with a right wrist sprain.
4066336:wrist.long: The star forward is missing a second consecutive contest, and he faces a short turnaround to return ahead of Wednesday's tilt against the Magic. Josh Green figures to draw a second straight start, while Brice Sensabaugh and Josh Okogie should see a bump in playing time.

4278129:leg.name: Deandre Ayton
4278129:leg.note: Ayton won't return to Saturday's game against the Thunder due to a lower leg injury.
4278129:leg.long: Ayton will end his evening with two points (1-2 FG), one rebound and one turnover in seven minutes. For now, he should be considered questionable for Monday's game in Detroit.

4702670:knee.name: Grant Nelson
4702670:knee.note: Nelson signed a two-way contract with the Nets on Friday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
4702670:knee.long: Nelson appeared in four regular-season games for the Nets during the 2025-26 campaign and will link up with the franchise again. He's expected to spend the bulk of his time with their G League affiliate to open the season.

2595516:shoulder.name: Norman Powell
2595516:shoulder.note: Powell (shoulder) is questionable for Friday's game against the Hawks.
2595516:shoulder.long: Powell is trying to avoid a third consecutive absence due to a shoulder injury. With rookie standout Caleb Wilson (hand) going on the shelf for multiple weeks, Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro both have a chance to step up for the Bulls.

4433627:illness.name: Keyonte George
4433627:illness.note: George (illness) has been downgraded to questionable for Sunday's game against Minnesota.
4433627:illness.long: George presumably woke up under the weather before being a late addition to the injury report. If the star point guard is unable to suit up, Darryn Peterson could see additional on-ball duties. Additionally, Isaiah Collier and Svi Mykhailiuk would be candidates for increased playing time.

4351852:illness.name: Mitchell Robinson
4351852:illness.note: Robinson (illness) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Kings, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
4351852:illness.long: Robinson is under the weather and will not play in the front end of Boston's back-to-back set, but he could be available for Sunday night's game against the Warriors. With Robinson sidelined, Luka Garza and Chris Cenac should both see a bump in minutes behind starting center Neemias Queta.

4277843:illness.name: Gary Trent Jr.
4277843:illness.note: Trent (illness) won't play in Sunday's game versus the Celtics.
4277843:illness.long: Trent will miss his fourth consecutive game Sunday. However, since he has totaled only 13 minutes in his two appearances this season, his absence won't have much of an effect on the rotation.

3032979:hamstring.name: Dennis Schroder
3032979:hamstring.note: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
3032979:hamstring.long: Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

3138196:lower-body.name: Cameron Johnson
3138196:lower-body.note: Johnson (lower body) is questionable for Monday's game against Houston.
3138196:lower-body.long: Johnson has already missed three games this season. If he is unavailable for a fourth time Monday versus the Rockets, it could mean more minutes for Spencer Jones and Alpha Diallo.

4431767:calf.name: Christian Braun
4431767:calf.note: Braun (calf/illness) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against Houston.
4431767:calf.long: Braun is under the weather and also dealing with a left calf contusion. Nikola Jokic (elbow), Jamal Murray (shin), Aaron Gordon (lower body), Cameron Johnson (lower body) and DeMar DeRozan (back) are all listed as questionable as well, so the Nuggets could be shorthanded Monday. If Braun is ruled out, Spencer Jones, Cam Whitmore and Bryce Hopkins would be candidates for increased minutes.

3936299:lower-leg.name: Jamal Murray
3936299:lower-leg.note: Murray is questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets due to a left shin contusion.
3936299:lower-leg.long: Murray could miss his first game of the season due to a right lower leg injury. If he is unavailable, Tyus Jones could see an expanded role.

3064290:lower-body.name: Aaron Gordon
3064290:lower-body.note: Gordon (lower body injury management) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets.
3064290:lower-body.long: Along with Nikola Jokic (elbow), Jamal Murray (shin), Christian Braun (calf/illness), Cameron Johnson (lower body) and DeMar DeRozan (back), Gordon is questionable to play Monday. If the veteran forward is unable to go, Trevon Brazile, Spencer Jones and Alpha Diallo would be candidates for increased playing time.

3112335:elbow.name: Nikola Jokic
3112335:elbow.note: Jokic (elbow) is listed as questionable for Monday's game in Houston.
3112335:elbow.long: Jokic nearly had a triple-double in Saturday's 114-102 win over the Pacers. However, he's now in danger of missing his first game of the 2026-27 season due to a right elbow sprain. If Jokic isn't available to suit up, Marvin Bagley would presumably take his place in the starting lineup.

4897262:thumb.name: Will Richard
4897262:thumb.note: Richard (thumb) has been upgraded to probable for Wednesday's game at Houston.
4897262:thumb.long: Richard is expected to play through a torn UCL in his left thumb. Over his last five games (two starts), the 23-year-old has averaged 5.2 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 18.2 minutes per tilt.

4397014:finger.name: Quentin Grimes
4397014:finger.note: Grimes (finger) said he expects to return to action Sunday against the Suns, according to Ricardo Sandoval of Lakers on SI.
4397014:finger.long: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games, but it sounds as if he could return to the rotation Sunday. It's unclear whether he'd be a starter, but he'd have a chance if Austin Reaves (heel) isn't cleared. Grimes is averaging 8.0 points per game this season, but that number rises to 17.5 points per game in his two starts.

3155942:knee.name: Domantas Sabonis
3155942:knee.note: Sabonis (knee) is questionable to play Tuesday's game against the Magic.
3155942:knee.long: Sabonis missed Sunday's 114-108 loss to the Heat with left knee soreness, making it his first absence of the season through 10 games. Dylan Cardwell earned the start with Sabonis sidelined, so if the latter is forced to miss a second straight contest, the former would be the top candidate to start once again.

4395630:groin.name: Devin Vassell
4395630:groin.note: Vassell is questionable for Friday's game against the Warriors due to left adductor tightness.
4395630:groin.long: Vassell is trying to avoid a third consecutive absence with the issue. Julian Champagnie would likely draw a third straight start at power forward for the Spurs on Friday if Vassell is unable to play.

4433627:ankle.name: Keyonte George
4433627:ankle.note: George (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Heat.
4433627:ankle.long: George sustained a right ankle sprain in Sunday's loss to Minnesota and will be sidelined for the front end of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against Orlando, and the 23-year-old's absence should open up additional minutes for guys like Isaiah Collier and Svi Mykhailiuk. Moreover, Darryn Peterson figures to take on additional on-ball duties.

4873153:leg.name: Morez Johnson Jr.
4873153:leg.note: Johnson (leg) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers.
4873153:leg.long: Johnson will miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign after tallying four points, nine rebounds and one assist in 19 minutes in the first half of a back-to-back set Sunday against Brooklyn. His absence could open up more minutes for Santi Aldama and Moussa Cisse behind starting center Daniel Gafford.

3134903:knee.name: Gary Payton II
3134903:knee.note: Payton (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against Houston.
3134903:knee.long: Payton is sidelined for a second consecutive contest with knee inflammation. Will Richard (thumb) could slot into Payton's spot in the backcourt rotation Wednesday.

4397040:hamstring.name: Brandon Williams
4397040:hamstring.note: Williams (hamstring) is out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
4397040:hamstring.long: Williams recently progressed to on-court work, but he will remain on the inactive list for Sunday's game. His next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Kings.

4432827:illness.name: Oscar Tshiebwe
4432827:illness.note: Tshiebwe has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Nuggets due to an illness.
4432827:illness.long: With Clint Capela (ankle) and Steven Adams (calf) sidelined, Tshiebwe has been able to appear in six straight games, averaging 6.8 minutes a night. With all three backup centers unavailable, Jabari Smith and Tari Eason might play some small-ball five minutes behind Alperen Sengun.

4845363:ankle.name: Cam Christie
4845363:ankle.note: Christie (ankle) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against Phoenix.
4845363:ankle.long: Christie will miss his fifth game of the 2026-27 campaign. The 21-year-old rookie has averaged only 6.0 minutes per contest in his five regular-season appearances, so his absence won't have much of an effect on the rotation.

4066457:illness.name: Austin Reaves
4066457:illness.note: Reaves (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Atlanta, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
4066457:illness.long: Reaves was added to the injury report earlier in the day after being diagnosed with an illness, and he's since been downgraded to out. This will mark his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign, presumably opening up opportunities for Collin Sexton and Cameron Carr.

4593016:head.name: Quinten Post
4593016:head.note: Post (concussion) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets.
4593016:head.long: Post suffered a concussion during Monday's 118-102 win over the Raptors, and now he will have to clear a series of steps before he's allowed to return to the court. Taylor Hendricks will help pick up the slack while Post is sidelined.

4395725:knee.name: Tyler Herro
4395725:knee.note: Herro (knee) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
4395725:knee.long: Herro is in jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest due to a right knee contusion. If the star guard remains on the inactive list, Ryan Rollins would likely stay in the starting five, while Kasparas Jakucionis could continue seeing increased burn off the bench.

4431675:ankle.name: Trendon Watford
4431675:ankle.note: Watford (ankle) is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
4431675:ankle.long: Watford can be considered week-to-week at this point until the Pelicans offer an update on his recovery. He hasn't played since Nov. 8 and is averaging just 7.2 points and 3.5 boards per game in his six appearances off the bench.

4395628:rest.name: Zion Williamson
4395628:rest.note: Williamson (rest) is out for Monday's game against the Warriors.
4395628:rest.long: The Pelicans are giving the star forward a maintenance day on the second half of this back-to-back, but Williamson should be able to play Wednesday against the Nets. With Trey Murphy (knees) also sidelined, Derik Queen, Saddiq Bey and Herbert Jones stand out as the most likely candidates to enter the starting lineup Monday.

4594327:wrist.name: Keegan Murray
4594327:wrist.note: Murray is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Magic due to right wrist soreness.
4594327:wrist.long: Murray made his return to court Sunday against Miami following a seven-game absence due to an ankle injury, and it now appears he's dealing with a wrist issue. The Kings will presumably monitor him closely during shootaround and warmups to determine if he can suit up Tuesday.

5093267:illness.name: Collin Murray-Boyles
5093267:illness.note: Murray-Boyles will not return to Wednesday's game against the Wizards due to an illness, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
5093267:illness.long: Murray-Boyles saw just four minutes of action before exiting due to an illness. Allen Graves and Kyle Anderson could see extra minutes with Murray-Boyles sidelined.

5104155:hand.name: Bilal Coulibaly
5104155:hand.note: Coulibaly (hand) is out for Monday's game against the Pistons.
5104155:hand.long: Coulibaly is missing his first game of the season Monday with a hand injury. Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington both make sense as streaming options for fantasy managers in the short term.

5105623:ankle.name: Kel'el Ware
5105623:ankle.note: Ware is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Knicks due to a left ankle sprain.
5105623:ankle.long: Ware was a late addition to the injury report, which is never a good sign, but the severity of the issue remains unclear. If the backup big man is unable to suit up, Jericho Sims, Nate Ament and Ousmane Dieng would be candidates for increased roles.

4702382:calf.name: Tristan da Silva
4702382:calf.note: Da Silva (calf) participated in Friday's morning shootaround and remains questionable for Friday's game against Milwaukee, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
4702382:calf.long: Da Silva has already missed multiple games due to the calf issue, but this is a step in the right direction. His participation in shootaround is a positive sign, but he'll still need to be cleared before Orlando can count on him for frontcourt minutes against the Bucks.

5279130:calf.name: Nolan Traore
5279130:calf.note: Traore (calf) is listed as probable for Saturday's game against Memphis.
5279130:calf.long: Traore appears on track to suit up despite dealing with discomfort in his right calf. The guard's expected availability should help Brooklyn maintain its backcourt depth, though his fantasy appeal remains dependent on his playing time and opportunities in the rotation. His status should be confirmed ahead of Saturday's tipoff.

5105555:back.name: Tobe Awaka
5105555:back.note: Awaka (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nets.
5105555:back.long: Awaka is missing a fifth straight contest due to a back problem. The rookie big man can be considered week-to-week going forward.

3062679:illness.name: Josh Hart
3062679:illness.note: Hart (illness) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers.
3062679:illness.long: Hart has missed three games in a row. First, he was sidelined for two contests due to a knee injury but didn't play Tuesday against the Bucks due to an illness. It appears he's moved past both issues and will return to action Wednesday. However, the veteran wing has been off to a slow start this season, averaging 8.6 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 2.1 steals in 31.6 minutes per game.

4431684:illness.name: Trayce Jackson-Davis
4431684:illness.note: Jackson-Davis is out for Thursday's game against the 76ers due to an illness.
4431684:illness.long: Jackson-Davis is missing both ends of Toronto's back-to-back set with the ailment. Jamison Battle should handle a larger role in the frontcourt Thursday.

4431679:lower-leg.name: Precious Achiuwa
4431679:lower-leg.note: Achiuwa (lower leg) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Celtics.
4431679:lower-leg.long: Achiuwa has missed three of the Kings' last four games while recovering from a left lower leg contusion, but there's a chance that the veteran forward is available for Saturday's contest. If he's cleared to play, then Dylan Cardwell would likely see a drop in playing time.

4251:illness.name: Paul George
4251:illness.note: George (illness) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Toronto, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
4251:illness.long: George will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set due to an illness, and his next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Mavericks. With the veteran forward sidelined, Baylor Scheierman, Sam Hauser and Hugo Gonzalez are all candidates to see increased playing time.

5101761:illness.name: Mikel Brown Jr.
5101761:illness.note: Brown (illness) has been upgraded to probable for Saturday's game at Memphis.
5101761:illness.long: After initially being listed as questionable due to an illness, Brown is trending in the right direction following a two-game absence. The rookie guard's return would leave fewer minutes available for Keon Ellis and Terance Mann. Brown has averaged 15.2 points, 3.8 assists and 2.0 rebounds in 24.6 minutes per tilt over his last five outings.

5095151:hip.name: Caleb Wilson
5095151:hip.note: Wilson has been downgraded to questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to right hip soreness.
5095151:hip.long: Wilson was a late addition to the injury report and will likely be a game-time decision ahead of tipoff at 8:00 p.m. ET. If the rookie forward isn't cleared to play, Leonard Miller and Noa Essengue would likely see increased playing time.

5037878:foot.name: Ugonna Onyenso
5037878:foot.note: Onyenso agreed to a two-way contract with the Pistons on Thursday.
5037878:foot.long: The No. 53 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Onyenso appears poised to see run in the G League after putting pen to paper on a two-way deal. He'll likely face an uphill battle to carve out a role in the rotation, so Detroit will presumably allow him to continue his development with Motor City.

3133628:rest.name: Myles Turner
3133628:rest.note: Turner has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers due to rest.
3133628:rest.long: Turner will miss his first game of the season after totaling only three points in 27 minutes during Tuesday's blowout loss in New York. In Turner's absence, Kel'el Ware and Jericho Sims are candidates for increased roles. Turner should return to action Friday in Orlando.

4683634:thumb.name: Bennedict Mathurin
4683634:thumb.note: Mathurin (thumb) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against Memphis.
4683634:thumb.long: Mathurin now has a better chance of suiting up after being listed as doubtful. The Pelicans are likely to re-evaluate the swingman closer to Friday's tipoff, but his status may not have a major impact on the rotation.

3136195:calf.name: Karl-Anthony Towns
3136195:calf.note: Towns (calf) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
3136195:calf.long: Towns may be held out of the second half of this back-to-back set due to a sore left calf. If the star big man is unable to play, Andre Drummond, Mohamed Diawara and James Wiseman would be candidates for increased playing time.

4066336:hand.name: Lauri Markkanen
4066336:hand.note: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
4066336:hand.long: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

4873153:lower-leg.name: Morez Johnson Jr.
4873153:lower-leg.note: Johnson (left shin contusion) is listed as probable for Saturday against Cleveland.
4873153:lower-leg.long: Johnson appears to be trending toward availability after recently missing one game due to the shin injury. The rookie has averaged 6.9 points and 4.8 rebounds in 16.7 minutes per game this season, limiting his appeal to deeper fantasy formats.

4396909:knee.name: Aaron Nesmith
4396909:knee.note: Nesmith (knee) is questionable for Friday's game against the Knicks.
4396909:knee.long: Nesmith picked up a knee injury during Wednesday's game against Washington, and he was ultimately unable to return after being diagnosed with knee soreness. He'll likely test his knee during shootaround and pregame to determine if he can take the court Friday.

4900671:ankle.name: Ajay Mitchell
4900671:ankle.note: Mitchell (ankle) is questionable to suit up for Sunday's game against the Kings.
4900671:ankle.long: Mitchell has missed OKC's previous two contests due to a sprained left ankle, and he's now in jeopardy of sitting out a third straight. If Mitchell remains sidelined, Jared McCain will continue to start for the 8-5 Thunder.

4278572:shoulder.name: Jamal Cain
4278572:shoulder.note: Cain (shoulder) participated in Friday morning's shootaround and remains questionable for Friday's game against the Bucks, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
4278572:shoulder.long: With Cain still carrying a questionable tag after shootaround and his availability still unsettled heading into Friday, his participation in morning practice is a step in the right direction. Cain is averaging 7.0 points on 19.5 minutes per game this season.

4706557:foot.name: Chris Youngblood
4706557:foot.note: Youngblood (foot) is out for Monday's game against the Timberwolves.
4706557:foot.long: Youngblood will miss a third straight game due to a right foot bone bruise. His next opportunity to suit up comes Tuesday against the Timberwolves.

5095151:hand.name: Caleb Wilson
5095151:hand.note: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5095151:hand.long: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

3975:abdomen.name: Stephen Curry
3975:abdomen.note: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
3975:abdomen.long: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

4277811:head.name: Collin Sexton
4277811:head.note: Sexton (head) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Suns, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
4277811:head.long: Sexton was a full participant in Saturday's practice, and while the questionable tag exercises some caution, he's trending in the right direction and could be available Sunday. The veteran has been putting up solid numbers of late, scoring in double digits in all but one of his last five appearances and averaging 11.0 points, 1.6 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game in that span.

4066457:heel.name: Austin Reaves
4066457:heel.note: Head coach JJ Redick said he expects Reaves (heel) to return for Monday's matchup with Utah or Friday's game in San Antonio, Mark Medina of TheSportingTribune.com reports.
4066457:heel.long: Reaves will miss his fourth straight game Friday, but it sounds like he'll be back next week. Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton will continue to pick up the slack while Reaves is out, and Luka Doncic will be operating with a hefty usage rate.

3945274:ankle.name: Luka Doncic
3945274:ankle.note: Head coach JJ Redick said Friday that Doncic (ankle) is "fine," per Law Murray of The Athletic.
3945274:ankle.long: The superstar guard exited to the locker room late in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's win over the Bucks due to an apparent right ankle injury and did not return. Doncic can be tentatively placed on the right side of the questionable marker until the Lakers release an official injury report at some point prior to Sunday's matchup in Phoenix.

4591725:head.name: Ryan Rollins
4591725:head.note: Rollins (head) exited to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's 123-112 loss to the Lakers and did not return, finishing with eight points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt), seven rebounds, four assists and one steal across 24 minutes.
4591725:head.long: Rollins bumped heads with Collin Sexton with 6:51 remaining in the contest, and both players exited to the locker room. Rollins' status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday's game at Orlando. If he needs to miss time, AJ Green and Kasparas Jakucionis could see increased playing time.

4601025:illness.name: Pelle Larsson
4601025:illness.note: Larsson won't play in Monday's game against the Rockets due to an illness, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
4601025:illness.long: Larsson, who came down with an illness last week, is a spectator for a third consecutive contest Monday. His continued absence should create another start for Myron Gardner and more playing time for Andrew Wiggins off the bench.

6475:ankle.name: Klay Thompson
6475:ankle.note: Thompson (ankle) is listed as probable for Saturday's game against the Pistons.
6475:ankle.long: Thompson missed the front end of this back-to-back set due to a left ankle sprain, though he's trending toward playing Saturday. If the veteran sharpshooter is cleared to play, there would be fewer minutes available for the likes of Ryan Conwell, Tim Hardaway and Myron Gardner.

4433268:ankle.name: Trey Alexander
4433268:ankle.note: Alexander won't play Wednesday against the Grizzlies due to a left knee bone bruise.
4433268:ankle.long: Alexander sat out Friday's preseason finale with what the team initially described as a left knee injury, but we now know he's dealing with a bone bruise. Don't be surprised if Alexander misses Friday's game against the Pelicans as well.

5149077:back.name: Kingston Flemings
5149077:back.note: Flemings (back) is questionable to play Sunday against the Pistons.
5149077:back.long: Flemings has missed the past three games, but it looks like there's a chance he could return Sunday. If he's cleared to play, Aaron Wiggins would likely head back to the second unit.

4432158:toe.name: Evan Mobley
4432158:toe.note: Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days.
4432158:toe.long: Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

4397886:toe.name: Charles Bassey
4397886:toe.note: Bassey is probable for Friday's game against the Spurs due to left toe soreness.
4397886:toe.long: It's not clear as to when this injury popped up for Bassey, who missed the first two games of the season with a knee issue but has been otherwise healthy. Expect the team to confirm his availability for Friday as tipoff nears.

2990992:suspension.name: Marcus Smart
2990992:suspension.note: Smart has been suspended three games for throwing a punch during Wednesday's matchup against Golden State, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
2990992:suspension.long: Smart, who was ejected from Wednesday's game for punching Charles Bassey, will begin serving his suspension Friday night against the Jazz, meaning he'll be eligible to return Wednesday versus Indiana. Bruce Thornton and Reed Sheppard should be in line for more minutes while Smart serves his three-game ban.

4593016:concussion.name: Quinten Post
4593016:concussion.note: Post (concussion) is questionable for Monday's game against the Wizards.
4593016:concussion.long: Post could miss a fourth consecutive game due to a concussion. Zach Edey (ankle) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) have also been deemed questionable, so Taylor Hendricks could see an expanded role.

4600663:ankle.name: Zach Edey
4600663:ankle.note: Edey (hip) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Warriors.
4600663:ankle.long: Edey is sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back. If healthy, Isaiah Stewart (illness) would draw the spot start at center in all likelihood.

4576086:elbow.name: Bryce McGowens
4576086:elbow.note: McGowens (elbow) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
4576086:elbow.long: McGowens will miss a fifth consecutive contest due to an infection in his left elbow. He's without a timetable to return and can be considered week-to-week until the Pelicans offer an update on his status.

4066259:hip.name: De'Aaron Fox
4066259:hip.note: Fox (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
4066259:hip.long: Fox has been dealing with left hip tightness recently, and it will finally force him to miss his first game of the season. He's playing 28.6 minutes a night, the lowest since his 27.8 mark during his rookie campaign in 2017, en route to averages of 13.6 points, 4.4 rebounds, 5.8 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 three-pointers across 13 games in 2026-27. Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper will handle the playmaking duties, while Julian Champagnie would be the top candidate to start in place of Fox.

4845374:chest.name: Bub Carrington
4845374:chest.note: Carrington (chest) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Houston.
4845374:chest.long: Carrington exited Thursday's loss to Detroit with a chest contusion and is now in jeopardy of missing his first game of the season. If the third-year guard is ruled out, Tre Mann and Will Riley could see increased burn, especially if Tre Johnson (back) is also downgraded from questionable to out.

3907497:ankle.name: Dejounte Murray
3907497:ankle.note: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
3907497:ankle.long: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

4431695:hand.name: Drew Timme
4431695:hand.note: The Suns claimed Timme off waivers Monday, per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com.
4431695:hand.long: After being let go by Minnesota on Saturday, Timme wasn't allowed to go through waivers unclaimed without Phoenix snatching him up. With Mark Williams (shoulder) likely out through the All-Star break, Timme helps reinforce Phoenix's depth at center.

4411057:illness.name: Kevin McCullar Jr.
4411057:illness.note: McCullar signed a two-way contract with the Raptors on Thursday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
4411057:illness.long: McCullar quickly finds a new home after being waived by the Knicks in late October. The forward is expected to play a prominent role for Toronto's G League affiliate.

5106268:back.name: Nae'Qwan Tomlin
5106268:back.note: Tomlin (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
5106268:back.long: Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

4432582:ankle.name: Max Christie
4432582:ankle.note: Christie (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
4432582:ankle.long: It's worth noting that Christie was a full practice participant Tuesday. His return from a two-game absence with an ankle sprain would likely lead to less playing time for Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher on the wing.

4396909:hand.name: Aaron Nesmith
4396909:hand.note: Nesmith (hand) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Philadelphia.
4396909:hand.long: Nesmith suffered a left hand sprain in the final seconds of Friday's win over the Knicks and could be held out of Sunday's road game. If the veteran swingman is unable to suit up, Jarace Walker, Quenton Jackson and Jalen Slawson would be candidates to see an uptick in minutes.

4397077:knee.name: Jaxson Hayes
4397077:knee.note: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Clippers.
4397077:knee.long: Hayes will miss a second consecutive game due to a left knee strain, with his next chance to suit up coming Wednesday in the second half of the Jazz's back-to-back set. Mo Bamba is likely to remain in the starting lineup after faring well in his first start Sunday. On the year, Hayes is averaging 8.8 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.3 blocks across 12 appearances (10 starts).

2595516:back.name: Norman Powell
2595516:back.note: Powell (back) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against Minnesota.
2595516:back.long: After erupting for 33 points in 31 minutes during Friday's overtime win over the Hawks, Powell is in danger of missing the second leg of this back-to-back set due to lower-back injury management. If the veteran guard is ruled out, Buddy Hield and Tre Jones could see increased burn.

3908809:knee.name: Donovan Mitchell
3908809:knee.note: Mitchell (knee) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
3908809:knee.long: Mitchell will miss his first game of the season due to a left knee contusion. The Cavaliers will be without all of their usual starters, meaning Tyrese Proctor, Meleek Thomas and Craig Porter should all see significant minutes in the backcourt.

3992:calf.name: James Harden
3992:calf.note: Harden (calf) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Dallas.
3992:calf.long: Harden will miss his first game of the season due to a calf issue he picked up sometime after Friday's loss to Miami. Fellow guard Donovan Mitchell (knee) will also be inactive Saturday, leaving Tyrese Proctor, Craig Porter and Meleek Thomas as Cleveland's top backcourt options.

2991070:head.name: Jerami Grant
2991070:head.note: Grant (head) is out for Saturday's game against the Nets.
2991070:head.long: Grant will miss the second leg of Memphis' back-to-back set due to a head injury. His absence should open up more opportunities for GG Jackson, Taylor Hendricks and Olivier-Maxence Prosper.

4065733:hip.name: Ty Jerome
4065733:hip.note: Jerome (hip) is probable for Saturday's game in Minnesota.
4065733:hip.long: Jerome is set to return from a three-game layoff Saturday, which will likely shift Cam Spencer back to the second unit. Jerome has gotten off to a hot start this season, averaging 25.4 points, 5.3 assists and 2.5 triples per contest on 48.5 percent shooting from the field and 90.2 percent at the line.

4594327:illness.name: Keegan Murray
4594327:illness.note: Murray (illness) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
4594327:illness.long: Murray didn't participate in Saturday's shootaround, so the questionable tag isn't a surprise. De'Andre Hunter and Dylan Cardwell could play a bigger role if Murray isn't available, especially since Precious Achiuwa (ankle) is also uncertain to suit up Sunday.

5160992:illness.name: Alex Sarr
5160992:illness.note: Sarr (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Houston.
5160992:illness.long: Sarr is under the weather and could miss the front end of this back-to-back set. The big man's absence would open up additional minutes for guys like Deandre Ayton, Anthony Gill and Will Riley.

5238230:back.name: Tre Johnson
5238230:back.note: Johnson (back) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against Memphis.
5238230:back.long: Johnson is in danger of missing a second consecutive contest due to lower-back soreness. If the second-year guard is ultimately ruled out, there would be more minutes available for the likes of Bub Carrington and Will Riley.

4278104:personal.name: Michael Porter Jr.
4278104:personal.note: Porter (personal) is out for Saturday's game against the Grizzlies, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
4278104:personal.long: Porter was handed a questionable tag Saturday afternoon and now won't suit up for this matchup in Memphis. This is a huge loss for Brooklyn, as Porter is averaging 21.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 1.3 steals per game this season. Keon Ellis, Terance Mann and Danny Wolf could all see more minutes with Porter out, while Julius Randle would be in line for a higher usage rate on offense.

4278049:face.name: Daniel Gafford
4278049:face.note: Gafford (face) won't return to Saturday's game against the Cavaliers, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports.
4278049:face.long: Gafford took a shot by Thomas Bryant and exited the game after making two free throws earlier, but the center won't return. This means Morez Johnson and Santi Aldama should see more time in the frontcourt. Gafford ends the contest with 10 points (4-5 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT), three rebounds and an assist across 17 minutes. His next chance to play will come Sunday against the Celtics on the second leg of a back-to-back set.

3157465:thigh.name: Duncan Robinson
3157465:thigh.note: Robinson (thigh) did not return to Saturday's 137-117 win over the Pistons. He finished with 10 points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and one assist across 17 minutes.
3157465:thigh.long: There haven't been any updates regarding the severity of Robinson's injury. However, he shouldn't be considered a lock to suit up against the Spurs on Tuesday night. If Robinson is unavailable for that contest, Ronald Holland and Kevin Huerter are candidates to receive more playing time, with one of those players potentially moving into the starting lineup.

4395712:hip.name: Andrew Nembhard
4395712:hip.note: Nembhard (hip) is questionable for Friday's game in Cleveland.
4395712:hip.long: Nembhard is battling a left hip injury. Head coach Rick Carlisle indicated that the 26-year-old wouldn't be out long, though it remains to be seen if he can get back on the floor Friday against the Cavaliers. If Nembhard misses a third consecutive contest, Quenton Jackson would presumably remain in the starting lineup.

5060631:ankle.name: Adou Thiero
5060631:ankle.note: Thiero (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Suns.
5060631:ankle.long: Thiero missed the first nine games of the season due to a knee injury, and he's now dealing with a sprained left ankle. If he's unable to suit up, Ziaire Williams and Sandro Mamukelashvili will likely soak up any vacated minutes.

5105550:foot.name: GG Jackson
5105550:foot.note: Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months.
5105550:foot.long: Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

4997526:finger.name: Ousmane Dieng
4997526:finger.note: Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports.
4997526:finger.long: Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

4432247:hamstring.name: Jaylen Clark
4432247:hamstring.note: Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks.
4432247:hamstring.long: Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

4683634:foot.name: Bennedict Mathurin
4683634:foot.note: Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
4683634:foot.long: Mathurin will miss a fourth straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the undermanned Pelicans moving forward, while Mathurin can be deemed week-to-week.

4576087:abdomen.name: Peyton Watson
4576087:abdomen.note: Watson (abdominal soreness) is questionable to play in Monday's game against the Bulls.
4576087:abdomen.long: Watson missed Saturday's 127-117 win over Dallas due to a hamstring injury, but he's now dealing with right abdominal soreness. Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas will see an uptick in minutes if Watson remains sidelined Monday.

4593125:ankle.name: Santi Aldama
4593125:ankle.note: Aldama (ankle) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
4593125:ankle.long: Aldama practiced fully Tuesday and should be able to play through an ankle sprain Wednesday. He's set to return from a one-game absence, which could result in fewer minutes for Morez Johnson.

4432810:illness.name: Isaiah Stewart
4432810:illness.note: Stewart is questionable for Thursday's game against the Warriors due to an illness.
4432810:illness.long: Memphis is likely to check back in with Stewart closer to tipoff. The big man has a golden opportunity Thursday to start if available, with Zach Edey (ankle) already ruled out for the second half of this back-to-bac.

4591725:illness.name: Ryan Rollins
4591725:illness.note: Rollins (illness) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game at Miami.
4591725:illness.long: Rollins wasn't included on the initial injury report, though he's since been ruled out for a second straight game due to an illness. His next chance to play will come Thursday versus Portland. With the 24-year-old combo guard sidelined, Kasparas Jakucionis and Gary Trent will likely continue seeing increased minutes.

4433134:out.name: Scottie Barnes
4433134:out.note: Barnes (groin) is listed as probable to play in Sunday's game against the Knicks.
4433134:out.long: Barnes has missed Toronto's previous four games due to a left groin strain, but it sounds like he's ready to make his return to the floor. He's averaging 23.5 points, 7.6 rebounds, 5.1 assists and 2.3 steals in 33.3 minutes across eight outings in 2026-27.

4997536:ankle.name: Gui Santos
4997536:ankle.note: Santos is questionable for Monday's game against New Orleans due to right ankle inflammation.
4997536:ankle.long: Santos appears to have put a lingering knee injury behind him, but he's now experiencing an issue with his right ankle. He'll presumably test the injury in shootaround and pregame to determine whether he can suit up for Monday's game.

4065732:hip.name: De'Andre Hunter
4065732:hip.note: Hunter (hip) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers.
4065732:hip.long: Hunter has been bothered by left hip soreness. While it kept him off the floor for Sunday's 125-103 loss to the Thunder, he returned for Wednesday's meeting with the Suns. If Hunter can't suit up Friday, it could mean more minutes for Leaky Black and Alex Karaban.

3064440:illness.name: Zach LaVine
3064440:illness.note: LaVine is out for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City due to illness, Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com reports.
3064440:illness.long: LaVine was ruled out shortly before tipoff after falling ill. Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk should be in line for additional opportunities Sunday with LaVine sidelined.

4397424:rest.name: Neemias Queta
4397424:rest.note: Queta (rest) won't play in Monday's game against the Magic, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
4397424:rest.long: The big man is sitting out the second half of this back-to-back set Monday, but he should be good to go for Wednesday's showdown in Denver. Mitchell Robinson is the most likely choice to replace Queta in the starting lineup, while Luka Garza should see a sizable chunk of the center minutes.

4684740:knee.name: Amen Thompson
4684740:knee.note: Thompson (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Pacers.
4684740:knee.long: Thompson is looking to end a one-game absence Wednesday due to a knee issue. Reed Sheppard has a chance to play a considerable role off the bench if Thompson sits out.

5105553:wrist.name: Julian Phillips
5105553:wrist.note: Phillips (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against Dallas.
5105553:wrist.long: Phillips will shake off his questionable tag for Wednesday's regular-season opener. However, the two-way player isn't likely to be part of the Rockets' rotation.

4997528:illness.name: Nikola Jovic
4997528:illness.note: Jovic (illness) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
4997528:illness.long: Jovic is trending in the right direction following a one-game absence due to an illness. However, his return wouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation.

4397189:undisclosed.name: Jalen Smith
4397189:undisclosed.note: Smith (undisclosed) exited in the fourth quarter of Monday's 126-115 loss to the Cavaliers and did not return.
4397189:undisclosed.long: Smith collided with Peyton Watson at the rim, and both players stayed down several minutes before eventually leaving the contest. Smith did return to the bench after initially going back to the locker room, but Chicago opted to keep him out for good with the tilt in its final stages. He had a stellar outing prior to his exit, finishing with 17 points (6-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks in 28 minutes. The Bulls will provide an update on his health when available.

4431687:finger.name: Patrick Williams
4431687:finger.note: Williams (finger) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Brooklyn.
4431687:finger.long: After suffering a dislocated right pinky finger in Monday's loss to the Cavaliers, Williams is expected to play Wednesday. The 25-year-old forward is averaging 7.8 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 0.8 steals across 22.7 minutes per contest in six regular-season appearances.

4576087:head.name: Peyton Watson
4576087:head.note: Watson left Monday's 126-115 win over Chicago due to a head injury and did not return.
4576087:head.long: As expected, Watson missed the remainder of Cleveland's victory after taking a nasty fall on a drive to the basket with a little more than five minutes left in the game. He recorded 14 points (5-10 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), four rebounds and one blocks across 22 minutes. We'll know more once the Cavs provide an update on Watson's status moving forward.

2990962:knee.name: Taurean Prince
2990962:knee.note: Prince (knee) underwent surgery to address lingering issues and has no timeline for a return, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
2990962:knee.long: With Detroit still without a return timetable for Prince after right knee surgery, he appears set for an extended absence well beyond Friday's tilt against Toronto. Prince hasn't been a significant part of the Pistons' rotation this season, so his continued absence is unlikely to create a major fantasy ripple effect.

4683771:knee.name: Ronald Holland II
4683771:knee.note: Holland (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Atlanta.
4683771:knee.long: Holland has missed the last three games due to a bone bruise in his left knee. If he remains sidelined versus the Hawks, Isaiah Joe, Chaz Lanier and Javonte Green are candidates for more minutes.

3157465:quadriceps.name: Duncan Robinson
3157465:quadriceps.note: Robinson will be re-evaluated in one week due to a left quadriceps strain, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
3157465:quadriceps.long: Robinson has gotten off to a strong start this season, though he's now expected to miss at least the next week after appearing in each of Detroit's first 12 regular-season games. The sharpshooter is averaging 17.4 points in 30.5 minutes per contest, and his absence will open up additional minutes for Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green.

4433136:lower-leg.name: Walker Kessler
4433136:lower-leg.note: Head coach JJ Redick said he expects Walker (leg) to be available for Wednesday's game against the Jazz, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
4433136:lower-leg.long: Walker won't play Tuesday against the Hornets due to some minor soreness in his right leg, but he'll return for the second leg of the back-to-back set Wednesday. Sandro Mamukelashvili, Jarred Vanderbilt and Kevon Looney will pick up the slack in his absence.

4066261:hip.name: Bam Adebayo
4066261:hip.note: Adebayo (hip) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Bucks, per Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel.
4066261:hip.long: The star big man was pulled as a precaution Monday against Houston due to a hip issue, and he's not expected to miss more time. After scoring in double figures in nine consecutive appearances prior to Monday's abbreviated outing, Adebayo will be aiming to start a new double-digit points streak Wednesday.

4433247:shoulder.name: Jonathan Kuminga
4433247:shoulder.note: Kuminga (shoulder) is questionable for Thursday's game against the Knicks, Charlie Walton of ZoneCoverage.com reports.
4433247:shoulder.long: After missing Tuesday's game against Portland, Kuminga now has a chance to return Thursday from a bruised shoulder. His status will affect Terrence Shannon's streaming appeal most prominently in fantasy leagues.

4397189:head.name: Jalen Smith
4397189:head.note: Smith (undisclosed) exited in the fourth quarter of Monday's 126-115 loss to the Cavaliers and did not return.
4397189:head.long: Smith collided with Peyton Watson at the rim, and both players stayed down several minutes before eventually leaving the contest. Smith did return to the bench after initially going back to the locker room, but Chicago opted to keep him out for good with the tilt in its final stages. He had a stellar outing prior to his exit, finishing with 17 points (6-9 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-3 FT), 11 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks in 28 minutes. The Bulls will provide an update on his health when available.

3917376:hamstring.name: Jaylen Brown
3917376:hamstring.note: Brown (hamstring) went through individual work during Friday's practice, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports.
3917376:hamstring.long: Brown is set to be re-evaluated this weekend due to a left hamstring strain, meaning his next chance to play will come Monday against Portland. Dean Wade (hamstring), Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker are all candidates for increased minutes while Brown is sidelined.

2490149:calf.name: CJ McCollum
2490149:calf.note: McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.
2490149:calf.long: The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.

4576087:back.name: Peyton Watson
4576087:back.note: Watson (back) is questionable for Friday's game against the Pacers.
4576087:back.long: Watson is looking to fight off a bruised back and suit up Friday. If the swingman is unable to give it a go, his absence could result in a second straight start for Mario Hezonja as well as an expanded role for Meleek Thomas.

4896372:ankle.name: Walter Clayton Jr.
4896372:ankle.note: Clayton (ankle) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
4896372:ankle.long: Clayton has only missed one game this season, and that's not expected to change Wednesday versus Golden State. The 23-year-old is coming off a strong showing, amassing 13 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal in Sunday's 131-94 loss to Boston. Clayton also logged 23 minutes, though he might not play as much Wednesday with Kyrie Irving (knee) off the injury report.

5106040:groin.name: Tobi Lawal
5106040:groin.note: Lawal (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
5106040:groin.long: Lawal will miss a third consecutive game due to a right groin strain. His absence won't have much of an impact on the Mavericks' rotation. Lawal's next chance to suit up will come Tuesday against Denver.

3213:back.name: Al Horford
3213:back.note: Horford (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Mavericks, but will play Thursday against the Grizzlies, Nick Friedell of The Athletic reports.
3213:back.long: Horford will miss the first half of a back-to-back set Wednesday due to a back injury, but will be available Thursday. Charles Bassey could see an expanded role in Horford's absence, while Horford could see a larger role than usual Thursday with Draymond Green set to rest.

4431772:hamstring.name: Myron Gardner
4431772:hamstring.note: Gardner (hamstring) is probable for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
4431772:hamstring.long: The probable tag suggests Gardner is on the verge of returning to the hardwood after a one-game absence due to injury. He's been in and out of the starting five, but he started his last three games before missing Wednesday's win over the Bucks. He's averaging 3.0 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game this season, so even if he's cleared to play Sunday, he shouldn't carry a ton of fantasy appeal.

4592979:quadriceps.name: Zyon Pullin
4592979:quadriceps.note: Pullin (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Knicks.
4592979:quadriceps.long: Pullin is battling a quad injury. However, he has averaged only 3.3 minutes in his three regular-season appearances during the 2026-27 campaign, so his status for Thursday's meeting with New York won't affect the rotation.

4683021:foot.name: Deni Avdija
4683021:foot.note: Avdija (foot) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Knicks.
4683021:foot.long: The star point forward is looking to avoid a three-game absence with a bruised left foot. Damian Lillard would do the heavy lifting offensively if Avdija is out, while Jayson Kent would be in line for a third consecutive start.

4706557:heel.name: Chris Youngblood
4706557:heel.note: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Knicks.
4706557:heel.long: Youngblood has been on the shelf since Nov. 10 due to a right heel bone bruise. Until Portland signals otherwise, Youngblood can be considered out indefinitely moving forward.

5105841:back.name: Felix Okpara
5105841:back.note: Okpara (illness) is available for Friday's game against Toronto.
5105841:back.long: Okpara will shed his questionable tag due to an illness and suit up Friday. However, the two-way player isn't guaranteed to see the floor.

3135045:concussion.name: Grayson Allen
3135045:concussion.note: Allen (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Atlanta.
3135045:concussion.long: Allen is currently dealing with concussion-like symptoms and is in line for a second straight absence. Sion James and Royce O'Neale should continue to see an uptick in playing time until Allen is cleared to return.

5037871:undisclosed.name: Dylan Harper
5037871:undisclosed.note: Harper left Tuesday's game against the Spurs due to an undisclosed injury after an awkward fall, Chris Mannix reports.
5037871:undisclosed.long: The injury occurred with only 53.6 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, and Harper stayed down in pain for several minutes before being helped back to the locker room. He tallied 20 points (8-14 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 4-5 FT), four rebounds and two assists in 35 minutes prior to his exit, and we'll have to wait for an update on his status moving forward.

4432166:knee.name: Cade Cunningham
4432166:knee.note: Cunningham (knee) is probable to play Sunday in Atlanta.
4432166:knee.long: Cunningham is dealing with some minor soreness in his right knee, but he's planning to play through it. Cunningham is averaging 25.6 points, 5.1 rebounds, 7.9 assists, 2.0 triples, 1.4 steals and 0.9 blocks per game this season.

3912848:hamstring.name: Dean Wade
3912848:hamstring.note: Wade (hamstring) won't play Saturday against the Bucks.
3912848:hamstring.long: Wade was able to get through a full practice Friday, but the 76ers' medical staff still isn't quite ready to clear him for game-time action. His next chance to play will come Monday against the Trail Blazers. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker will continue to help pick up the slack while Wade is sidelined.

4395625:hamstring.name: RJ Barrett
4395625:hamstring.note: Barrett has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
4395625:hamstring.long: Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

4871144:eye.name: Alperen Sengun
4871144:eye.note: Sengun (eye) is questionable for Friday's game against the Nuggets.
4871144:eye.long: Sengun suffered a blow to the face during Wednesday's game against Indiana, and his availability is now in jeopardy for Friday's tilt. The Rockets should have another update on the big man closer to tipoff.

4431678:foot.name: Tyrese Maxey
4431678:foot.note: Maxey (foot) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Bucks.
4431678:foot.long: Maxey sat out Wednesday's 121-116 win over the Magic, but he was a full participant at Friday's practice, so he's trending in the right direction. If Maxey is cleared to return, Anfernee Simons would likely head back to the second unit and VJ Edgecombe's usage rate would dip.

4431736:rest.name: Toumani Camara
4431736:rest.note: Camara is questionable to play Thursday against the Bucks due to general soreness.
4431736:rest.long: Camara is in danger of missing his first game of the season due to general soreness. If he's forced to the sidelines, his minutes will be divvied up amongst Siddy Cissoko and Jrue Holiday.

5037871:hip.name: Dylan Harper
5037871:hip.note: Harper (hip) is expected to miss two to three weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
5037871:hip.long: Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain, and San Antonio is now set to be without one of its regular guards for an extended stretch. His absence creates more backcourt minutes for the Spurs, likely most prominently for Justin Champagnie while the team waits for Tobias Harris (calf) to make his season debut. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle should see extra ball-handling duties as well.

5105854:ankle.name: Braden Smith
5105854:ankle.note: Smith (ankle) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against Cleveland.
5105854:ankle.long: Smith tweaked his ankle during Wednesday's matchup against Washington, and he's now in danger of missing Friday's action. Quenton Jackson could be asked to pick up a few additional minutes if Smith is unable to take the court Friday.

2991350:hip.name: Alex Caruso
2991350:hip.note: Caruso (hip) won't play Sunday against the Heat.
2991350:hip.long: Sunday will mark Caruso's second straight game on the sidelines, but maybe he'll be able to get back out there for Monday's meeting in Indiana. Bennett Stirtz and Nique Clifford will help pick up the slack in Caruso's absence.

4702670:ankle.name: Grant Nelson
4702670:ankle.note: Nelson (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Orlando.
4702670:ankle.long: Nelson will hit the inactive list due to a sprained right ankle. The two-way player's absence shouldn't affect the rotation.

4433149:back.name: LJ Cryer
4433149:back.note: Cryer (back) is questionable for Thursday's game against Memphis.
4433149:back.long: Cryer is at risk of missing the second half of this back-to-back set. De'Anthony Melton could be moved into a larger role if Cryer is sidelined.

3134907:shoulder.name: Kyle Kuzma
3134907:shoulder.note: Kuzma (shoulder) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Portland due to a right shoulder contusion.
3134907:shoulder.long: Kuzma's absence further depletes Milwaukee's frontcourt, with Myles Turner (shoulder) also sidelined. Bobby Portis could see increased offensive opportunities, while additional minutes may become available to the team's reserve forwards. Kuzma's next opportunity to play comes Saturday against Philadelphia, depending on his recovery.

3133628:shoulder.name: Myles Turner
3133628:shoulder.note: Turner (shoulder) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Portland due to a left shoulder contusion,
3133628:shoulder.long: Turner will miss Thursday's contest after playing 21 minutes against Miami on Wednesday. His absence leaves Milwaukee without its primary rim protector and could create additional frontcourt opportunities for Bobby Portis and the team's reserves. Turner's next opportunity to return will come Saturday against Philadelphia, pending further injury updates

5242496:wrist.name: Noa Essengue
5242496:wrist.note: Essengue is listed as probable for Friday's game against Washington due to bilateral wrist soreness.
5242496:wrist.long: Essengue is expected to suit up Friday despite dealing with soreness in both of his wrists. He's logged double-digit minutes in back-to-back games and has averaged 5.4 points and 3.4 rebounds in 12.3 minutes per tilt across eight appearances in November.

5258459:oblique.name: Ebuka Okorie
5258459:oblique.note: Okorie (oblique) is out for Sunday's game in Atlanta.
5258459:oblique.long: This will be Okorie's second straight game on the inactive list due to injury. His next chance to play will come Tuesday in Orlando.

2991235:quadriceps.name: Steven Adams
2991235:quadriceps.note: Adams (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against Denver.
2991235:quadriceps.long: The right quad contusion is a new concern for Adams, who has appeared in two of Houston's last three outings following an 11-game absence due to a right soleus strain. If the big man joins Clint Capela (ankle) on the inactive list, Oscar Tshiebwe, Jabari Smith and Tari Eason would be candidates for increased playing time.

2991070:calf.name: Jerami Grant
2991070:calf.note: Grant (calf) is out for Saturday's game against the Timberwolves.
2991070:calf.long: Grant went down early in Thursday's win over the Warriors, and he's now dealing with a strained left calf that could cost him multiple contests. With Cameron Boozer (ankle) also sidelined, Taylor Hendricks and Olivier-Maxence Prosper are both worthy of streaming consideration in fantasy leagues.

5093267:concussion.name: Collin Murray-Boyles
5093267:concussion.note: Murray-Boyles (concussion) participated in Sunday's practice, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
5093267:concussion.long: Murray-Boyles missed Friday's win over Detroit while in the league's concussion protocol, though it's encouraging to see him back at practice. The Raptors should offer an update on his status for Monday's game against the Bucks by Sunday night.

4397189:illness.name: Jalen Smith
4397189:illness.note: Smith (illness) has been upgraded to probable for Sunday's game against the Nuggets.
4397189:illness.long: Smith was initially listed as questionable but is now expected to return from a one-game absence due to an illness. Over his last five appearances, the big man has averaged 17.2 points, 8.2 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.2 blocks across 28.2 minutes per showing. He could also see a slight bump in minutes if Nic Claxton (illness) is ruled out.

5159925:hip.name: Nikola Topic
5159925:hip.note: Topic (hip) is listed as out for Sunday's game versus the Heat.
5159925:hip.long: Topic has appeared in only three games for Oklahoma City this season. He will now miss a second consecutive contest due to a hip injury, with his next opportunity to play coming Monday versus the Pacers. Considering Topic has averaged just 11.3 minutes per outing, his absence won't have much of an effect on the rotation, though he might have seen more action if Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (back/neck), who is questionable, can't suit up.

3078576:shoulder.name: Derrick White
3078576:shoulder.note: White (shoulder) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against Sacramento.
3078576:shoulder.long: White drew the questionable tag for Saturday's game due to left AC joint sprain in his shoulder. The veteran guard will be in street clothes for the first leg of the Celtics' back-to-back set, but he could make his return Sunday against the Warriors. With Jayson Tatum (rest) also out, Payton Pritchard and Paul George will carry the workload for the Celtics, and there will be more opportunities for the likes of Sam Hauser, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman and Jordan Walsh.

4433287:ankle.name: Brandon Miller
4433287:ankle.note: Miller amassed 28 points (10-19 FG, 5-12 3Pt, 3-3 FT), two rebounds, four assists and one block in 32 minutes during Tuesday's 118-114 overtime loss to the Lakers.
4433287:ankle.long: Miller bounced back from a miserable shooting night against the Clippers and led Charlotte in scoring, though a costly turnover in the final seconds of regulation helped open the door for the Lakers' rally. Efficiency has been an issue for the forward all season, so this was one of his better shooting performances. With Kon Knueppel (hamstring) sidelined, Miller remains the focal point of the Hornets' offense.

4278078:shoulder.name: P.J. Washington
4278078:shoulder.note: Washington (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game versus the Clippers.
4278078:shoulder.long: Washington has had a productive 2026-27 campaign thus far, averaging 14.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.1 blocks over 30.8 minutes per outing. He has also appeared in all 15 of the Mavericks' regular-season games, though he is in danger of missing Saturday's meeting with the Clippers. If Washington gets ruled out, more minutes should open up for Zaccharie Risacher and Naji Marshall.

4896372:knee.name: Walter Clayton Jr.
4896372:knee.note: Clayton (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
4896372:knee.long: Clayton is in danger of missing the second leg of this back-to-back set due to left patellar tendinitis. The two-way player has logged at least 23 minutes in five of the last six games, and if he's forced to miss Sunday's contest, Marcus Sasser and Max Christie would likely see increased playing time.

4781746:personal.name: Javon Small
4781746:personal.note: Small won't play Saturday against the Timberwolves due to personal reasons.
4781746:personal.long: It's unclear exactly what Small is dealing with, but for now, he can be considered questionable for Monday's meeting in Charlotte. With Small out, Cam Spencer and Jahmai Mashack will fill the minutes behind Ty Jerome.

5041935:ankle.name: Cameron Boozer
5041935:ankle.note: Boozer is out for Saturday's game against Minnesota due to a right ankle sprain.
5041935:ankle.long: The rookie sensation is sitting out for the first time this year and can be deemed day-to-day for the time being. His absence puts a ton of pressure on Ty Jerome (hip), who's set to return from a three-game layoff, and opens up a spot in the starting lineup likely for Isaiah Stewart.

2528426:foot.name: Jordan Clarkson
2528426:foot.note: Clarkson (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Indiana.
2528426:foot.long: Clarkson will miss a third consecutive game due to plantar fasciitis in his right foot. In his absence, Tyler Kolek and Jose Alvarado should see an uptick in playing time off the Knicks' bench. Clarkson's next chance to suit up will come Wednesday against Cleveland.

3934719:calf.name: OG Anunoby
3934719:calf.note: Anunoby (calf) won't play Sunday against the Pacers.
3934719:calf.long: Anunoby will miss a second straight game due to left calf tightness. Landry Shamet got the start in Saturday's 97-96 win over Portland, so fantasy managers should expect the same versus Indiana. Anunoby's next chance to suit up will come against the Cavaliers on Wednesday.

5279130:hamstring.name: Nolan Traore
5279130:hamstring.note: Traore (hamstring) won't return to Friday's game against Orlando, Meghan Triplett of YES Network reports. He finished with four points (2-6 FG, 0-2 3Pt) and two assists over 18 minutes.
5279130:hamstring.long: After a drive to the rim in the fourth quarter, Traore was observed holding the back of his right hamstring in obvious discomfort. He limped to the locker room and was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the contest. Mikel Brown and Egor Demin are in line for more minutes the rest of the way.

4888725:quadriceps.name: Ryan Dunn
4888725:quadriceps.note: Dunn (quadriceps) was a full participant in Sunday's practice, Duane Rankin of The Arizona Republic reports.
4888725:quadriceps.long: Dunn exited Friday's win over Utah early due to a right quad injury, though it's encouraging that he was able to practice Sunday. The Suns will provide an update on his status for Monday's game at New Orleans by Sunday night.

4065733:out.name: Ty Jerome
4065733:out.note: Jerome (hip) is probable for Saturday's game in Minnesota.
4065733:out.long: Jerome is set to return from a three-game layoff Saturday, which will likely shift Cam Spencer back to the second unit. Jerome has gotten off to a hot start this season, averaging 25.4 points, 5.3 assists and 2.5 triples per contest on 48.5 percent shooting from the field and 90.2 percent at the line.

3136195:illness.name: Karl-Anthony Towns
3136195:illness.note: Towns (illness) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Pacers.
3136195:illness.long: Towns missed Saturday's 97-96 win over Portland due to an illness, and that same ailment could force him to miss a second consecutive game. Andre Drummond got the start in Towns' place while James Wiseman saw a season-high 25 minutes off the bench. If Towns is forced to sit again Sunday, expect a similar approach for New York.

2595516:hamstring.name: Norman Powell
2595516:hamstring.note: Powell has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated later this week.
2595516:hamstring.long: Powell sustained the hamstring injury in Friday's loss to the Wizards and is now set to miss at least the next two contests. With the veteran swingman on the shelf, Isaac Okoro, Buddy Hield, Tre Jones and Patrick Williams are all candidates for increased playing time.

4278078:illness.name: P.J. Washington
4278078:illness.note: Washington (illness) is doubtful to play Sunday's game against the Jazz.
4278078:illness.long: Washington is in danger of missing a second straight contest due to an illness. Zaccharie Risacher started in place of Washington during Saturday's 110-100 win over the Clippers, and that is likely to be the case again versus Utah.

3149673:hip.name: Pascal Siakam
3149673:hip.note: Siakam (hip) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against New York.
3149673:hip.long: Siakam has only missed one game this season, but he's in danger of sitting out Sunday due to left hip soreness. If the 32-year-old can't suit up versus the Knicks, Obi Toppin may move into the starting lineup.

3032977:groin.name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
3032977:groin.note: Antetokounmpo (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City, Ira Winderman of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
3032977:groin.long: Antetokounmpo previously dealt with a wrist injury in November, and he's now working through a groin issue that puts his status for Sunday's game up in the air. He has yet to miss a game this season, but if he's not cleared to play against Oklahoma City, then Andrew Wiggins and Bobby Portis would be the top candidates to enter Miami's starting lineup.

4395628:thigh.name: Zion Williamson
4395628:thigh.note: Williamson is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs due to a left thigh contusion.
4395628:thigh.long: Williamson won't suit up Saturday on the second leg of this back-to-back set. Derik Queen will start in his place alongside Yves Missi in the frontcourt. This will be Williamson's second absence this season. The 26-year-old is averaging 21.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.8 steals across 32.4 minutes per outing in 16 regular-season games.

4278073:back.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
4278073:back.note: Gilgeous-Alexander (back/neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus Miami.
4278073:back.long: After scoring 40 points in Friday's 126-120 win over the Pelicans, Gilgeous-Alexander could miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign due to back and neck issues. With Nikola Topic (hip), Alex Caruso (hip) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) all unavailable, Bennett Stirtz may be needed in the starting lineup if Gilgeous-Alexander is ruled out Sunday.

4431687:thumb.name: Patrick Williams
4431687:thumb.note: Williams is probable for Sunday's game against the Nuggets due to a left thumb sprain.
4431687:thumb.long: Williams is dealing with a sprained thumb on his non-shooting hand, but he's expected to play through it. Williams is averaging 6.9 points and 1.9 assists per game this season.

4278067:illness.name: Nic Claxton
4278067:illness.note: Claxton (illness) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Nuggets.
4278067:illness.long: After missing the first eight outings of the 2026-27 campaign due to a hamstring injury, Claxton has suited up in six of the last seven games for Chicago. However, he's now dealing with an illness that will leave his status for Sunday up in the air. If Claxton doesn't play, expect Zach Collins and Noa Essengue to earn more minutes off the bench.

4845374:illness.name: Bub Carrington
4845374:illness.note: Carrington (illness) has been downgraded to questionable for Sunday's game against the Magic.
4845374:illness.long: Carrington was a late addition to the injury report due to an illness. If the third-year guard is unable to play Sunday, Tre Johnson could see a slight bump in minutes. Carrington has seen limited playing time of late, totaling just eight minutes in two appearances over Washington's last three games.

4278129:illness.name: Deandre Ayton
4278129:illness.note: Ayton (illness) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against Orlando.
4278129:illness.long: Ayton played 11 minutes during Friday's 98-94 win over Chicago, but he appears to have picked up some sort of illness over the weekend. If he can't play Sunday, expect Khris Middleton and Bilal Coulibaly to see increased burn off the Wizards' bench.

5209602:coach-s-decision.name: Matilde Villa
5209602:coach-s-decision.note: Villa (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against New York.
5209602:coach-s-decision.long: Villa signed with Atlanta on Sept. 15 but will end the campaign without having seen any game action. She's ineligible to play in the postseason while on a developmental pact.

3058895:leg.name: Brionna Jones
3058895:leg.note: Jones will miss the remainder of the season after sustaining a left leg injury against the Sun on Aug. 13, Annie Costabile of The Athletic reports.
3058895:leg.long: This is a tough blow for a Dream team that is sitting in second place in the Eastern Conference. Jones managed to play in just nine games this campaign, finishing with averages of 8.2 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists. Look for the Dream to use a committee approach to soak up those minutes going forward.

4066548:foot.name: DiJonai Carrington
4066548:foot.note: Carrington (foot) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Mystics.
4066548:foot.long: Carrington will end the season on the inactive list for a fifth consecutive contest due to a left foot injury. She'll finish the campaign having averaged 8.8 points, 3.1 rebounds, 0.6 assists and 0.6 steals in 16.2 minutes per game across 11 regular-season outings. She's set to enter unrestricted free agency this offseason following an injury-riddled year.

4433433:knee.name: Aicha Coulibaly
4433433:knee.note: Coulibaly (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Mystics
4433433:knee.long: Coulibaly's rookie year comes to an end due to a knee injury. She'll be looking to take a step forward next year after averaging 5.2 points, 2.6 rebounds and 0.7 steals per game this year for the Sky.

3142010:knee.name: Azura Stevens
3142010:knee.note: Stevens (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Mystics
3142010:knee.long: Steven is sidelined Thursday with a knee injury, ending her regular season. The veteran forward is under contract with the Sky for 2027, and she averaged 10.6 points, 6.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.8 blocks per game in 2026.

2529137:knee.name: Natasha Cloud
2529137:knee.note: Cloud (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Mystics.
2529137:knee.long: Cloud is out for the season finale Thursday with a knee injury. The veteran guard is slated to be an unrestricted free agent this winter, having averaged 11.1 points, 4.8 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game for the Sky this year.

2491205:knee.name: Skylar Diggins
2491205:knee.note: Diggins (knee) will miss the remainder of the 2026 WNBA season, Sara Jane Gamelli of BallisLife.com reports.
2491205:knee.long: She will now "focus on recovering an aggravated right knee injury." She hadn't played since July 3 and her rehab didn't progress as quickly as she would've hoped. She appeared in 19 games and posted averages of 14.2 points, 3.2 rebounds and 4.9 assists.

4433630:knee.name: Rickea Jackson
4433630:knee.note: The Sky announced Tuesday that Jackson will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL in her left knee during Sunday's 86-79 win over the Lynx.
4433630:knee.long: The season-ending knee injury is a devastating development for Jackson and the Sky, as the 25-year-old forward was well on her way to a career-best campaign. Through Chicago's first four games, Jackson averaged 18.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 29.5 minutes per contest. After Jackson's early exit in Sunday's contest, Aicha Coulibaly opened the second half with the starters and looks to be the most likely candidate to move into the top unit for the Sky's next game Wednesday versus the Wings.

4433792:knee.name: Rayah Marshall
4433792:knee.note: Marshall has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's game against the Tempo due to a right knee injury.
4433792:knee.long: Marshall suffered a knee injury shortly after checking in and won't be able to continue in this one. Nell Angloma could see a few more minutes in Marshall's absence.

4398966:knee.name: Olivia Nelson-Ododa
4398966:knee.note: Nelson-Ododa (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Tempo.
4398966:knee.long: Nelson-Ododa is sidelined for the regular-season finale with a knee injury. She has one more year left on her deal after averaging a career-high 10.1 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists for the Sun in 2026.

4433514:ankle.name: Saniya Rivers
4433514:ankle.note: Rivers (ankle) is out for Thursday's game against the Tempo.
